title: Special Positions in a Binary Matrix
summary: Determine the count of special positions in a binary matrix.
statement: Determine the count of special positions in a binary matrix. A position (i, j) is special if the element at mat[i][j] is 1 and all other elements in row i and column j are 0.
constraints: A special position contains one and is the only one in both its row and column.
Return the number of special positions.
hints: Precompute each row sum and column sum.
Count it exactly when its row and column sums are both one.
Those two equalities are precisely the definition of no other one in either direction.
editorial: Those two equalities are precisely the definition of no other one in either direction.

tests.explanation: The one at row one, column two is alone in both its row and column.
Every diagonal one is alone in its row and column, giving three.
